simple.meaning: נָפַשׁ (nâphash) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to breathe ; passively, to be breathed upon , i.e. (figuratively) refreshed (as if by a current of air).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Exodus, 2 Samuel, beginning at Exodus 23:12. Its contexts include family line, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָפַשׁ (H5314).

definitions.short: to breathe ; passively, to be breathed upon , i.e. (figuratively) refreshed (as if by a current of air)
definitions.full: H5314. naphash [ נָפַשׁ ] verb denominative (compare Syriac refresh ; , be refreshed ; Ethiopic ); — Niph`al Imperfect 3masculine singular יִנָּפֵשׁ Exod 23:12 (E) 2Sam 16:14 ; וַיִּנָּפַ֑שׁ Exod 31:17 (P); — take breath, refresh oneself.

occurrences.englishText: “Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, that your ox and your donkey may have rest, and the son of your servant, and the alien may be refreshed.
It is a sign between me and the children of Israel forever; for in six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.’ ”
The king, and all the people who were with him, came weary; and he refreshed himself there.
